how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.17: It works well for people who attend many meetings and mainly need to know what they personally must do, and a 2-by-2 table in Word, Google Docs or a notebook is all it takes. Long, context-heavy discussions? Less useful there; Cornell or outline layouts suit those better.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.28: The person taking notes should not be the person running the meeting, since facilitating and writing at the same time means both get done badly. Rotate the role. That way the burden does not always land on one person.
how-to-take-good-meeting-notes.16: The quadrant method splits a page into 4 boxes: **decisions**, **my actions**, **others' actions** and **questions or notes**. Each point goes straight into its box, so the page is already organized when the meeting ends.
